status.en: 5 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Rumbek, Central Equatoria State and Western Equatoria State.
status.nb: 5 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Rumbek, Central Equatoria State og Western Equatoria State.

summary.en: Intercommunal clashes in Rumbek have killed at least 71 people, including soldiers, and prompted the caretaker governor Rin Tueny to return to Lakes State. The violence follows the killing of the Akobo commissioner by unknown assailants and the sentencing of a soldier to ten years for murdering a UN worker. A drone strike by the RSF killed 41 people in Sudan's Blue Nile region, a development mentioned alongside the South Sudan clashes. The conflict now shows a sharp increase in lethal communal violence compared with the two battle-related deaths recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
